transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Sparkline CTO), Amrita Shah (Sparkline ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Sparkline FinOps)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown (the "cost map"), and how Redwood Optimize suggestions reduce spend. Customer is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated; primary drivers are latency for chat triage (sub-second SLOs for triage path), and predictable billing for compliance audits. Team asked about VPC/private control plane for PHI workloads and encryption (KMS) details.

Topics covered:
- Route snapshot (per-route throughput, p50/p95 latency, error rates)
- Cost map (token-level and route-level allocation, chargeback)
- Optimize recommendations: batching, quantization suggestions by route
- Security briefly: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs

Action items noted during call (also in metadata): Jesse to seed sandbox & sample dashboard; Priya to run perf estimate; Marcus to send volumes.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jesse: all right hi everyone uh thanks for joining, I'm Jesse from Redwood Inference. quick intros?
[00:10] Marcus: hey Marcus here, CTO at Sparkline. we got Amrita and Tom on — Amrita runs ML infra, Tom handles our FinOps.
[00:18] Amrita: hi, yes.
[00:20] Tom: hey all.
[00:22] Jesse: cool. Priya and I will walk the console, focus on per-route and cost map. we'll try to keep it practical.
[00:30] Priya: hi all, i'll start with the route snapshot view — it's the single pane we open to see how your routes are performing and spending. Note: some auto captions call it "route snap" in older versions, so if you saw that earlier it's the same.
[00:45] [screen share noise — brief pause]
[00:52] Priya: ok so first row here is the route list — each route is an API path you configure, for sparkline you might have /triage-chat, /summarize-notes, /embed-index. you can pin critical routes to the top.
[01:10] Marcus: do routes map 1:1 to internal endpoints? we have many microservices — can they map to tags or labels?
[01:19] Priya: yes, you can apply labels and group rules. we also ingest a route tag from the SDK header — so minimal code changes. sometimes the transcriber writes K V cash instead of KV cache, just FYI.
[01:30] Amrita: ha, i've seen that.
[01:32] Priya: each route card shows p50/p95 latency, tokens per request, requests per minute, and an estimated cost-per-request based on your model mix. here's the cost map button — it breaks down spend by tokens, model family, and route.
[01:50] [mouse click sound]
[01:53] Priya: opening cost map — top-left is token distribution by route, center is model attribution (e.g. Llama-3/Redwood-16/Alpaca-v2 if used), bottom is a chargeback-ready view that exports CSV for your billing system.
[02:12] Tom: that CSV export — can we map it to our chargeback center codes? we need that for monthly internal invoices.
[02:20] Jesse: yes we can add custom mapping keys. we'll include an example in the sandbox.
[02:25] Marcus: can the cost map split cached vs compute costs? we use a prefix cache heavily for summarize-notes.
[02:33] Priya: good question — we show effective token counts and separately show cache hits. the console labels cached tokens and shows delta to uncached cost. sometimes the auto transcript calls it "KV cash hits" instead of cache hits, you'll see that in older exports.
[02:48] Amrita: what about burst / dedicated capacity? our triage path spikes during clinic hours.
[02:55] Priya: two parts — Dedicated pools give you reserved throughput and consistent tail latency; console will show capacity utilization and autoscale events. for cost planning, the cost map will show dedicated commit amortized per route when you allocate capacity to a route.
[03:12] Tom: ok helpful — can you show us Optimize suggestions? we want to reduce per-ticket cost without hurting quality.
[03:20] [scrolling]
[03:23] Priya: here's Optimize — it suggests batching for low-latency-safe routes, quantization profiles for internal models, and model-switching policies by route. for example, summarize-notes is a good candidate for int8 quantization which reduces token cost ~30% in our estimate.
[03:40] Marcus: what's the impact on latency for quantized models? we need p95 under 800ms for triage chat.
[03:47] Priya: quantized models often slightly reduce throughput on some GPUs but our policy suggests using quantization for non-critical routes; for triage-chat we recommend a smaller model variant or Dedicated pool to keep p95 tight. i'll note a perf estimate here.
[03:59] Jesse: Priya will run a perf estimate based on your triage path size — Amrita can share the typical token lengths.
[04:06] Amrita: sure, we average 320 tokens for triage, but summaries run 900–1,200 tokens.
[04:13] [typing]
[04:15] Priya: perfect, that helps. i'll run a quick estimate for 320-token p95.
[04:20] Marcus: security — we need VPC private control plane for PHI. do you support that? and KMS integration?
[04:28] Jesse: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-controlled VPC and on-prem. we integrate with AWS KMS/GCP KMS and HSMs via our enterprise plan. we'll drop the security brief and the network diagram in the follow-up.
[04:40] Tom: do you retain transcripts or tokens by default? audit requires minimal retention.
[04:45] Jesse: default hosted has 30-day logs but you can change retention or opt for no-retention policies on Private/Dedicated. audit logs and SSO/SAML events are available.
[04:55] Amrita: audit logs format — can we stream them to our SIEM?
[04:59] Priya: yes we provide export hooks to your S3 or to syslog endpoints.
[05:05] [pause; brief side conversation about time zones]
[05:20] Priya: back to the console — i'll filter the route table by error rate > 1% and show a recent spike. you can click on a route to see request traces and prompt snapshots. note that prompt snapshots are redacted by default for PHI-sensitive routes unless you enable secure traces.
[05:40] Marcus: how do you handle PII redaction?
[05:43] Jesse: we have both client-side and server-side redaction options; for PHI we recommend client-side tokenization plus Private deployment.
[05:52] Priya: here's the per-route quality monitor — it ties evals to a prompt set, shows regressed prompts, and flags output drift. that way if a new model increases hallucinations on summarize-notes we detect it immediately and can auto-roll back.
[06:08] Amrita: auto-rollbacks — is that per-route? can we canary to a small percentage?
[06:13] Priya: yes canary rollouts per route, and automatic fallback to a compatibility variant if SLA breaches.
[06:20] Tom: back to cost map — if we want to do internal showback monthly, can you surface cost per feature slider in the UI?
[06:27] Priya: yes there's a cost allocation editor — you can create buckets and map routes. we'll include a sample mapping for "Triage" and "Summaries" in the sandbox.
[06:36] Marcus: any native integrations with our billing system? we use ChargeOps.
[06:40] Jesse: we have CSV exports and webhooks; for deeper integration we can work with engineering. many customers build a small adapter.
[06:48] Amrita: curious — what's typical savings customers see from Optimize suggestions?
[06:51] Priya: it varies, but we typically see 20–40% on cost-heavy summaries when batching, cache and quantization are tuned. for chat-first workloads savings are lower unless you switch models or add dedicated pooling.
[07:05] [brief cross-talk]
[07:10] Marcus: timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in November, production Q1. any blockers?
[07:15] Jesse: sounds doable. next steps: we'll provision a sandbox with sample routes and dashboards, Priya will attach perf estimates, and we'll send security docs.
[07:25] Tom: can we get a Dedicated pricing ballpark for 3-month commit?
[07:29] Jesse: yes — i'll include a ballpark in the follow-up; for formal quotes we'll loop finance.
[07:34] Amrita: one last thing — do you support per-route model pinning? we want summaries pinned to the latest vetted model while chat uses a rollback-safe variant.
[07:42] Priya: yep per-route pinning and model versioning is supported. we show rollouts and can revert in the console.
[07:48] [wrap-up sound]
[07:50] Jesse: recap: sandbox + dashboard by 10/24, security docs and network diagram, perf estimate for 320-token triage, ballpark Dedicated pricing.
[07:59] Marcus: thanks, this was useful. we'll send route volumes by tomorrow.
[08:04] Tom: thanks everyone.
[08:06] Jesse: thanks all, we'll follow up with the links. bye.
